7.0.0.en: Now after these things: that is, after the first return of the Jews to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel, and after the building of the temple, which was completed in the reign of King Darius, and after the reign of King Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther, Artaxerxes the son of Ahasuerus became king, and his reign was from 464 to 424 BC. This was a long period, during which took place the last part of the Book of Ezra (chs. 7-10) and also the whole Book of Nehemiah.

7.0.1.en: These verses set out Ezra's priestly lineage, which reaches back to Aaron the high priest in the days of Moses. In this chain we see some important figures such as:

7.0.2.en: 1- Seraiah: He was the grandfather of Ezra, not his father, and he was the high priest who was killed, among 70 of the most important men of Jerusalem, at the Babylonian attack on it, its destruction and the burning of the temple (2 Kgs 25:18-21).

7.0.3.en: 2- Hilkiah: the high priest in the days of King Josiah, who found the book of the Law in the house of the Lord (2 Kgs 22:13).

7.0.4.en: 3- Phinehas: the priest who killed the Israelite and the Moabite woman with whom he committed adultery, and by this the wrath of God was appeased in the face of this great immorality in the temple of God (Num 25:8). This chain does not contain all of Ezra's forefathers, but the most important of them were chosen; fifteen persons are mentioned here, but the complete chain contains 30 priests.

7.0.5.en: Ezra was a priest and not a high priest, but he was a scribe who cared about copying the Law of God, so he understood it and was able to explain its meanings. The scribes were few, and therefore they were highly esteemed; that is, Ezra had a great standing as a spiritual leader, in addition to his being the leader of the second company of those returning to Jerusalem.

7.1.0.en: Ezra the priest did not practice his priestly work, because he lived in Babylon, and God blessed him, so he obtained the position of a scribe in the court of the Persian king Artaxerxes, which was an important position.

7.1.1.en: In addition to this, Ezra took care to write the Law and was skilled, not only in writing it but also in understanding the Law, so that he was able to be an expounder of it to the Jews around him.

7.1.2.en: But how did the Law of Moses reach Babylon? There are many possibilities, among them:

7.1.3.en: 1- The captives carried it from Jerusalem to Babylon when they were taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar.

7.1.4.en: 2- When Nebuchadnezzar seized the vessels of the house of the Lord and everything in it, he may have found among them the book of the Law and carried it with the vessels, and Ezra discovered it afterward, because he worked in the royal court, so he cared for this copy and began to copy from it, read it and understand it.

7.1.5.en: Since God saw Ezra's heart that loved Him, his care for the Law and the worship of the Lord, and his longing to practice his priestly service in Jerusalem, He blessed him, helped him and gave him the desire of his heart, making his return to Jerusalem easy for him, and King Artaxerxes agreed to this and encouraged him with many reinforcements. We feel the blessing of God with Ezra in the repetition of the phrase "the hand of the Lord upon Ezra", which is mentioned six times in (chs. 7, 8), and this means God's love and obedience and Ezra's love for His commandments.

7.2.0.en: The Nethinim: They were Gentiles from Gibeon who joined the people of God in the days of Joshua, and he made them drawers of water and hewers of wood for the service of the temple. They loved the God of Israel, so they returned from captivity to serve His house. A great number of Jews went up with Ezra to Jerusalem from Babylon, nearly eight thousand, and they were from the different classes of the people; some were priests and others were servants of the temple, such as the Levites, the singers, the porters and the Nethinim.

7.2.1.en: The return of Ezra and those with him to Jerusalem was in the seventh year of Artaxerxes Longimanus, and this king loved the Jews, so Ezra returned in his days, and thirteen years after him Nehemiah returned by order of the same king.

7.2.2.en: The return of the Jews from Babylon to Jerusalem took place in three stages: the first under Zerubbabel, the second under Ezra and the third under Nehemiah, so that God would give an opportunity to everyone who loves Him and loves His house to return to Jerusalem. God wants everyone to return and encourages them, so whoever could not return with the first company has an opportunity with the second or the third. We see the hand of God that encouraged the kings Cyrus and Artaxerxes and prepared the hearts of His children Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah, in order to encourage as many as possible to return to Him. But the people's response was weak because of their attachment to the material things of the world. They loved the world more than God and remained in captivity, enduring bondage for the sake of worldly possessions and lusts.

7.3.0.en: The caravan moved under the leadership of Ezra from Babylon to Jerusalem; it set out in the first month and arrived at the beginning of the fifth month, that is, the journey took four months, in which the faith of Ezra and the Jews and their reliance on God appeared, because they did not ask the king for a guard. On the other hand, the care of God and His preservation of His children appeared, until they arrived in peace at the holy city of Jerusalem. The distance they covered on this journey was about 900 miles.

7.4.1.en: Judgments: rulings, that is, commandments and laws.

7.4.2.en: Ezra took care to read the Law, understand it and meditate on its meanings, so his heart clung to it. After this he practiced this Law in his life and held to it with all exactness, so the Jews saw him and learned from him the keeping of the Law. Then Ezra was able to teach the people the Law, and they received it easily from him, because they had seen it first in him, and God blessed him greatly for his faithfulness in these three stages: keeping, practicing and then teaching. What is beautiful in Ezra is that he cared for the Law, kept it and practiced it in Babylon, far from the house of the Lord. He loved God although he was surrounded by pagans, so when he arrived in Jerusalem he was encouraged and was very distinguished in practicing the Law and teaching it.

7.4.3.en: Take care to read the Bible every day and meditate on it, so that you can apply it in your life as a personal message to you in your life, and then you can be a light to the world and teach the word of God, and people will accept it from you.

7.5.0.en: King Artaxerxes supported Ezra the scribe, who worked for him, with a royal letter containing great orders for the care of the house of the Lord, in which the strong hand of God appears, which moved the king to support Ezra and those returning with him from captivity.

7.5.1.en: Artaxerxes styles himself king of kings, because he was an emperor who reigned over 127 provinces, among them the province of the Jews (Esth 1:1). This means that he was the greatest man in the world at that time, since he ruled the largest number of lands. He styles Ezra a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect peace, so he is not merely a scribe for the king but in addition he is the scribe of the law of God. This shows his esteem for Ezra. He styles God the God of heaven, the perfect, and this shows his esteem for God, for in his view He is not a god like the rest of the gods, but distinguished in that He is the God of heaven and that He is perfect. His esteem for God gives greater standing to His scribe, who is Ezra, and this is the first time a pagan king has styled God perfect.

7.5.2.en: Ezra was the chief of the scribes of the Law. He began his work in captivity and continued afterward in Jerusalem, and remained a scribe for eighty years, and he was distinguished by being both a scribe and a priest.

7.6.0.en: It appears in these two verses that Artaxerxes is the one who sent Ezra to inquire about and care for the Jews, and it was not Ezra who asked the king, as happened in the case of Nehemiah. This was of course by the providence of God, who moved the king to love the God of the Jews and call Him the God of heaven, the perfect, and to ask the blessing of this God and care for the welfare of His people who believe in Him.

7.6.1.en: The order issued is from the king and his seven counselors, and this was a system known among the Persians, which we also see with Ahasuerus the father of Artaxerxes (Esth 1:14). The number seven was honored among the Gentiles. These counselors were heads of fathers in Persia and represented a council that issued the royal orders under the leadership of the king, for it was the highest council in the empire and the ruling council.

7.6.2.en: Ezra was commissioned with authority from the king to care for the Jews, and at the same time he carried out the Law of God with all its reward and punishment, for by the authority of the king he executes and judges by the Law. This shows the king's trust in Ezra in addition to his trust in the Law of God.

7.6.3.en: The Jews could not have imagined a better situation than this for the application of the commandments and laws of God. Consequently Ezra had the right to appoint judges and governors under him to carry out the Law of God, supported by the order of the emperor Artaxerxes.

7.6.4.en: By the king's choosing Ezra and commanding him to apply the Law of God, he was able to win the Jews and secure their loyalty to him, since they would be ruled by one of their own and by the law of their God, a distinguished and wise man, a priest and scribe who understood the Law of God.

7.6.5.en: God commanded Ezra to take with him whoever wished of the priests, the Levites and the people to return with him to Jerusalem, and in this he supports the service of the house of the Lord and its worship and shows his love for the Jews.

7.7.0.en: After Artaxerxes commanded Ezra to visit and care for the Jews in Jerusalem and to make sure of their adherence to the Law of God, this is the first item of the order of Artaxerxes, which is mentioned in (vv. 13, 14). The second item is that Ezra should take with him the gold and silver that the king and his seven counselors had freely offered to the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem. This means the esteem, respect and faith of Artaxerxes and his counselors in God and their submission to Him as a great God. The wonder appears here in the submission of the chiefs of the Gentiles to God and their honoring of His house at the time when the Jews and their kings neglected the care of the house of the Lord, as happened before the captivity.

7.7.1.en: The third item in the king's order is the collection of contributions of silver and gold from the Gentile inhabitants of the land of Babylon, in addition to what he collects from the Jews in captivity in the land of Babylon, whether priests, Levites or the rest of the Jews. Here the king's concern appears that all his people should submit and care for the house of the Lord and revere God. The wonder is that he alerts the Jews who remained in captivity out of attachment to their possessions and whose hearts were not moved to go and worship their God in Jerusalem, or at least to contribute to the house of the Lord; for if Artaxerxes had been a Jew he would not have said more than this for the care of the house of the Lord.

7.7.2.en: May you be ashamed when you see the reverence of some unbelievers for your Church, your Christ and your saints, so that your heart may be moved, you may live for God, be committed to your worship and honor the saints.

7.8.0.en: The fourth item in the order of Artaxerxes is the purchase of livestock with the silver and gold to be offered as sacrifices to God in His temple at Jerusalem, in addition to the rest of the offerings and drink offerings of wine. The fifth item in the king's order is giving Ezra freedom to buy with the rest of the silver and gold whatever he sees that the temple needs, for the king wants the worship in the temple to go on in the best way. We notice here the following:

7.8.1.en: 1- Giving Ezra freedom as he sees the service to need, so that he may arrange it with all care.

7.8.2.en: 2- The king's concern for consultation among the leaders of the Jews for the arrangement of the service of the temple, because the king himself follows consultation in leading the kingdom of Persia, as he had seven counselors.

7.8.3.en: 3- The king's concern for the Law of God and His will, so he asks Ezra that they do everything in accordance with the will of God, that they may gain His satisfaction.

7.9.0.en: The king's concern to honor God appears in his offering precious vessels of silver and gold, or any other valuable materials, in addition to the vessels that the Jews and the Gentiles contributed to the house of the Lord. All this Ezra hands over to those responsible for the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, to be at their disposal for carrying out the service of the house of the Lord.

7.9.1.en: These vessels are not the vessels of the house of the Lord that returned with Zerubbabel, but precious vessels that were contributed to the house of the Lord.

7.10.0.en: The sixth item in the king's order is that Ezra may draw what he needs of money, in addition to the service of the house of the Lord, from the king's treasuries in the region beyond the river, and the king issued an order to those in charge of these treasuries to give Ezra what he asks of money and also what he asks of wheat, wine, oil and salt in large quantities as he needs, even if it reaches:

7.10.1.en: 1- A hundred talents of silver, equal to about 3,000 kilograms.

7.10.2.en: 2- A hundred cors of wheat, equal to about 150,000 kilograms.

7.10.3.en: 3- A hundred baths of wine, oil and salt, equal to 2,300 liters.

7.10.4.en: We see the king's concern in his order to the treasurers to give quickly all that Ezra asks, for he is concerned to provide the service of the house of the Lord as quickly as possible, and this is great love and esteem for God.

7.11.0.en: We see in this verse the following:

7.11.1.en: 1- The king's feeling that all he does is by the commands of God, that is, that the king is an instrument in the hand of God carrying out His will, which is a living, practical faith in God.

7.11.2.en: 2- The fear of God in the king's heart, for he wants to please God so that He will not be angry with him.

7.11.3.en: It is strange that the people of God did evil in the eyes of God, so captivity fell upon them, while the pagan king fears God and carries out His orders exactly. And after the return from captivity the Jews bound themselves in pagan marriages, contrary to the Law of God, while the pagan king in Babylon submits to the orders of God and fears Him. It should have been the opposite, because the people of God dwell in Jerusalem where the temple is, and the worship of God and the fear of Him should have influenced them more than the king.

7.11.4.en: At this time a rebellion took place in Egypt, so Artaxerxes sent soldiers to subdue it, and he wanted God's satisfaction with him so as to establish his kingdom and his sons' after him.

7.12.0.en: The seventh item in the king's order is the lifting of taxes from the priests and the servants of the temple, because they are consecrated to the service of the house of the Lord so that they might devote themselves to His service without care or other financial responsibilities, and this is of course a great honor to God, His house and His servants.

7.13.0.en: The eighth item in the order of Artaxerxes is that Ezra should choose rulers and judges from the Jews who know the Law of God, so that they may teach the people how to worship God and please Him in all their life. He also commanded him to take care to teach the rulers and judges, that they might complete their knowledge of the Law of God. Ezra is the head responsible for the learning of the people, so he teaches a group, the rulers and judges, with all exactness, so that they may teach the rest of the people.

7.13.1.en: Here we see the king walking in the thought of the New Testament, which the Didascalia expresses: "Wipe out iniquity by teaching", so he cares for teaching the people before punishing them when they sin, and the king directs Ezra to walk in this thought.

7.14.0.en: The ninth and last item in the king's order is the severe punishment of every Jew who violates the Law of God, according to the kind of his violation, either by death, or banishment to a far place where he suffers loneliness, or imprisonment, or payment of a fine.

7.14.1.en: From this we understand that Ezra was a religious leader who had the right to punish whoever violated the Law, but he was not a governor responsible for civil offenses, or for non-Jews. From the order of King Artaxerxes to Ezra we see his great trust in him, which shows us many qualities that were all gathered in his person, namely:

7.14.2.en: 1- The king commanded Ezra to inquire about those returning from captivity, out of trust in his fatherly care (v. 14).

7.14.3.en: 2- He gave him the silver and gold, confident of his faithfulness (vv. 15, 16).

7.14.4.en: 3- He granted him freedom to dispose of the silver and gold, confident of his wisdom (v. 18).

7.14.5.en: 4- He gave him the authority to take what he needed of money and foodstuffs from the king's treasuries in the region beyond the river, out of trust in his contentment (vv. 20, 21).

7.14.6.en: 5- He charged him with appointing rulers and judges to guide the people, confident of his good administration (v. 25).

7.14.7.en: 6- He asked him to take care to teach these rulers and judges and all the people, confident of his knowledge and his ability to teach (v. 25).

7.14.8.en: 7- He also gave him the authority to punish offenders with the various punishments, confident of his justice (v. 26).

7.15.s.en: (3) The work of God in the second return

7.15.0.en: When Ezra received this great letter from Artaxerxes he felt that he was before divine gifts he had never imagined, so he praised God, saying "Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers", remembering the love of God, who fulfills His covenants to the fathers, so He forgives His people despite the multitude of their sins when they repent, and gathers them from the dispersion of the world to worship Him in His temple at Jerusalem.

7.15.1.en: Ezra did not build the house of the Lord but he beautified it, not with drawings and ornaments but by organizing the service of the priests and Levites, teaching them with the people the Law of God, and his care for the continuation of the service with all exactness every day before the Lord.

7.16.0.en: Ezra thanked God for the grace He gave him in the eyes of the king and the great divine mercy in the king's order to him to return with the Jews to Jerusalem. Ezra had not asked the king, but it was the king who commanded him to do this, and of course that was because God moved the king's heart.

7.16.1.en: Ezra did not ascribe the work and the glory to himself in the return to Jerusalem, but ascribed it to the hand of God working in the king and in him, and he is truly a great man because of his great humility.

7.16.2.en: We also notice Ezra's energy and enthusiasm in seizing this opportunity, that is, the king's order, so he strengthened himself and gathered those of the Jews who wished to return and led them, with all the gifts he was able to gather, to Jerusalem.

7.16.3.en: How beautiful it is to thank God for His daily blessings to you! He is a tender Father always caring for you, and His gifts toward you never cease if you are spiritually watchful, so become accustomed to thanksgiving until your inner eyes are enlightened and you discover His providence and care for you.

7.16.4.en: The second return to Jerusalem under Ezra

7.16.5.en: 1- We notice in the return of the Jews to Jerusalem that none of the kings, Cyrus or Artaxerxes, commanded that all the Jews be compelled to return, because God respects man's freedom and waits for man to choose by himself to return to God.

7.16.6.en: 2- The return was in three groups to show the extent of the response of the people and the priests, for some hastened with Zerubbabel and others after a period, then the last were with Nehemiah, as Christ mentioned in the parable of the laborers, some at the first hour and others in successive hours until the eleventh hour.

7.16.7.en: 3- The leaders were different: Zerubbabel was of royal descent, Ezra was of the priests, and Nehemiah was of the people and obtained a position in Persian society, for God accepts all in His service with the variety of their abilities.

7.16.8.en: 4- Each company that returned to Jerusalem had a role:

7.16.9.en: a - The first company built the temple.

7.16.10.en: b - The second company organized the service in the temple.

7.16.11.en: c - The third company built the walls of Jerusalem and its gates.

7.16.12.en: Thus the roles of the companies were complementary in working for the good of the people and their relationship with God, and all took care of inward reform.

7.16.13.en: 5- The hand of God appears in this chapter, accompanying His people and preserving them until they reached Jerusalem from the land of Babylon, so that they might begin to thank God and worship Him.

7.16.14.en: 6- With the end of the previous chapter the writing in the Aramaic language ends, because the preceding chapters contain royal letters, and from this chapter Ezra begins to write in the Hebrew language, because he addresses the Jewish people, who are fluent in Hebrew.

7.16.15.en: (1) The heads of the fathers who returned (vv. 1-14)

7.16.16.en: 1- These are now the chief of their fathers, and this is the genealogy of them that went up with me from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king.

7.16.17.en: 2- Of the sons of Phinehas; Gershom: of the sons of Ithamar; Daniel: of the sons of David; Hattush. 3- Of the sons of Shechaniah, of the sons of Pharosh; Zechariah: and with him were reckoned by genealogy of the males an hundred and fifty. 4- Of the sons of Pahathmoab; Elihoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males. 5- Of the sons of Shechaniah; the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred males. 6- Of the sons also of Adin; Ebed the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males. 7- And of the sons of Elam; Jeshaiah the son of Athaliah, and with him seventy males. 8- And of the sons of Shephatiah; Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him fourscore males. 9- Of the sons of Joab; Obadiah the son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen males. 10- And of the sons of Shelomith; the son of Josiphiah, and with him an hundred and threescore males. 11- And of the sons of Bebai; Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty and eight males.

7.16.18.en: 12- And of the sons of Azgad; Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him an hundred and ten males. 13- And of the last sons of Adonikam, whose names are these, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them threescore males. 14- Of the sons also of Bigvai; Uthai, and Zabbud, and with them seventy males.

7.16.19.en: 1- At the end of the previous chapter Ezra tells us of his return with those of the Jews who accepted to return to Jerusalem. In this verse he tells us of the heads of the fathers returning to Jerusalem and mentions their details in the following verses.

7.16.20.en: 2- Ezra's concern was to write down the heads of the fathers, because each head would bring those who followed him from his clan, and so he mentions to us a large group of clans from which people returned.

7.16.21.en: 3- If we add up the numbers of those returning mentioned in these verses, we find 1,496, to which is added an unknown number referred to in (v. 2), so the estimated number of the men returning was about 1,700 men. If we add to them the women and children, the number is about eight thousand.

7.16.22.en: 4- The returning priests are mentioned at the beginning (v. 2) because of their importance in the service of the house of the Lord.

7.16.23.en: 5- It is mentioned in (v. 13) "the last sons of Adonikam" because a large number of his sons returned with Zerubbabel, and here we find 60 other men returning with Ezra, so it is understood from this that from the same clans a part returned in the first company and some in the second company.

7.16.24.en: God rejoices at your returning to Him, even if you have delayed in returning and been hindered, and did not go up with Zerubbabel. Now you have an opportunity to return with Ezra, that is, to return to Him with repentance and spiritual zeal to hold fast to His commandments and spiritual practices.

7.16.26.en: 15- And I gathered them together to the river that runneth to Ahava; and there abode we in tents three days: and I viewed the people, and the priests, and found there none of the sons of Levi. 16- Then sent I for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan, and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, men of understanding. 17- And I sent them with commandment unto Iddo the chief at the place Casiphia, and I told them what they should say unto Iddo, and to his brethren the Nethinims, at the place Casiphia, that they should bring unto us ministers for the house of our God. 18- And by the good hand of our God upon us they brought us a man of understanding, of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel; and Sherebiah, with his sons and his brethren, eighteen; 19- And Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, his brethren and their sons, twenty; 20- Also of the Nethinims, whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinims: all of them were expressed by name. 21- Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God, to seek of him a right way for us, and for our little ones, and for all our substance. 22- For I was ashamed to require of the king a band of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy in the way: because we had spoken unto the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all them for good that seek him; but his power and his wrath is against all them that forsake him. 23- So we fasted and besought our God for this: and he was intreated of us. 24- Then I separated twelve of the chief of the priests, Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brethren with them, 25- And weighed unto them the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, even the offering of the house of our God, which the king, and his counsellors, and his lords, and all Israel there present, had offered: 26- I even weighed unto their hand six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver vessels an hundred talents, and of gold an hundred talents; 27- Also twenty basons of gold, of a thousand drams; and two vessels of fine copper, precious as gold. 28- And I said unto them, Ye are holy unto the LORD; the vessels are holy also; and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering unto the LORD God of your fathers. 29- Watch ye, and keep them, until ye weigh them before the chief of the priests and the Levites, and chief of the fathers of Israel, at Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD. 30- So took the priests and the Levites the weight of the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem unto the house of our God.
